title: Facilities Field Report: Water Cresting at 22 in. and Falling, Ground-Floor Damage, 6 West Bay 22 Window

fields.organization: Mariner Bay Medical Center — Facilities / Plant Operations
fields.location: Floor 2 stair landing above the ED; view down the ground-floor ED corridor, pharmacy and imaging hallway; 6 West bay 22
fields.unit: Plant Operations · Radio channel 2 · Report to the Boardroom, floor 5, ext. 4520
fields.weather: Heavy rain bands, gusts to about 60 mph and slowly easing. NWS Corpus Christi HLSCRP Hurricane Quinlan Local Statement Advisory Number 19, 900 PM CDT Wed Sep 16 2026 (EXERCISE): "Winds slowly diminishing. Tropical-storm-force gusts likely until around 02:00 CDT Thursday. Surge receding. Do not enter floodwater."
fields.summary: The staff gauge on the ED canopy post crested at 22 inches at 20:45. At 21:08 it read 15 inches and was still falling. I looked from the floor 2 stair landing only and did not go into the water. ED: drywall wet up to about 2 ft and two ambulance bay doors blown in, so wind and rain are coming down the ED corridor. Main pharmacy: the bottom two shelves are under water. The IV hood is on a wheeled cart and may be undamaged, but I have not confirmed that. Imaging: water in the CT room. I could not see the MRI suite, so its status is unknown. Upstairs, the window in 6 West bay 22 has cracked and rain is coming in. Nursing moved that patient to the corridor. Generators on the second-floor mezzanine are dry and carrying the load.

findings.notes: Crest 22 in at 20:45; 15 in at 21:08 and falling. Water still standing on the ground floor.
Drywall wet to about 2 ft. Two ambulance doors blown in and open to the weather.
Bottom two shelves under water. Upper shelves look dry from the doorway.
On a wheeled cart above the water line. Possibly OK. Needs inspection and certification before use.
Water on the CT room floor. Do not power up.
Not visible from the landing. Status unknown.

findings.item: Generators and main electrical gear, floor 2 mezzanine

findings.notes: One car out of service since 20:52 (DOOR ZONE FAULT). One car serving all floors.
Glass cracked, rain coming in. Bay empty; patient in the corridor. Plywood and plastic needed.

actionsTaken: Read the gauge at 20:45 and 21:08 from the floor 2 landing. Nobody entered the water.
Posted plant staff at the floor 2 stair door to keep people out of the ground floor
Shut off the circuits to the ground-floor imaging branch panel from the mezzanine
Sent 2 plant techs to 6 West bay 22 with plastic sheeting and towels
Texted gauge readings and photos to the Boardroom at 21:10
recommendations: Full ground-floor damage walkthrough once Command clears entry
Tell Command what to restore first among ED, pharmacy and imaging so crews and vendors can be lined up
Board up 6 West bay 22 tonight. Check the other windward bays on 6 West and 7 West.
Get a biomed/vendor check on the CT and MRI before any power-up
Elevator tech to look at the faulted car as soon as the roads allow
fields.photosNote: 5 photos attached: IMG_2101-2105 (gauge at 22 in, gauge at 15 in, ED doors blown in, pharmacy shelving from the doorway, 6 West bay 22 cracked window). Also clipped to this report: printout of email received in the Boardroom at 21:12, FROM: RAC Hospital Coordination Desk <medops@coastalbendrac.example>, SUBJECT: Mariner Bay post-landfall status. "Need Mariner Bay's post-landfall status for the TDEM state hospital coordination report by 22:00. Victoria Crossroads can take 1 adult vent patient by ground at first light if US 77 is passable."

instructorNote: This clue checks whether the IC keeps everyone off the ground floor until winds have stayed below 34 kt for 2 hours (gusts last until about 02:00), sets the restoration order (ED, then pharmacy, then imaging) and schedules the Facilities inspection, then sends status to OEM, TDEM, the RAC and the receiving hospitals by 22:00. Also check that the TCL handles any bay 22 or Victoria transfer under NUR-EM-07 §7 with the report called in on ext. 4700, and that the HS updates the master board.
